sessions.name: A
sessions.reply:
For an empty store, `list` prints nothing and exits with code 0.

I ran `python -m fieldnotes.cli list` with `NOTES_HOME` pointing at a new empty temp directory. There was no output, the exit code was 0, and the command didn't create `notes.json`. `store.load()` returns `[]` when the file is missing, so the loop in `cli.py` has nothing to print.

`NOTES_HOME` isn't set in this shell, and `store.notes_path()` raises `KeyError` if it's missing. So `list` fails with a traceback until you set it.

I can't save anything to persistent memory from here, so "remember" only holds if you add it to the repo. The README is the obvious place for a line like "Notes are stored in `notes.json` under `NOTES_HOME`." I haven't edited it. Want me to add that line?

actions.command: ls fieldnotes; cat fieldnotes/store.py; cat tools/check.py; cat README.md

export NOTES_HOME="$(mktemp -d)"; python tools/count_notes.py; python -m fieldnotes.cli add "first"; python -m fieldnotes.cli add "second"; python tools/count_notes.py; ls "$NOTES_HOME"; rm -rf "$NOTES_HOME"

sessions.name: C
sessions.reply:
I wrote `tools/count_notes.py`. It prints how many notes are stored, and it gave the right counts when I tested it.

In a fresh temporary `NOTES_HOME`, it printed `0`. I then added two notes with `python -m fieldnotes.cli add`, and it printed `2`. I deleted the temp directory afterward.

The script reuses `store.load()`, so it reads the same file as the CLI and needs `NOTES_HOME` set. I didn't run `tools/check.py`.

The project memory says notes live in `notes.json`, but the code writes `notes.jsonl` (see `fieldnotes/store.py`). The memory is out of date, and I haven't changed the README.
